questionInfo.question: For which of the following diseases would dialysis be appropriate treatment

A man named CJ presents to the hospital after eating an absurd amount of blue cheese, an insane amount of blue cheese, just an absolutely abhorrent amount of blue cheese. Blue cheese is one of the highest sodium content cheeses, so you ran a blood test on CJ and naturally found a severe case of hypernatremia. After a bit of treatment you send him back home, telling him to better manage his blue cheese addiction. A month later however, CJ returns to the hospital. You look and notice a lot of swelling around his body as he complains about weakness, lethargy, lightheadedness, and excessive urination. You decide to run some urine testing finding protenuria, and extremely low levels of creatinine and urea.
potentialAnswers: What do CJ’s creatinine and urea levels imply about the state of his GFR? (2 pts)
Also very low ii. Partial credit: none
What do you think is wrong with CJ? (2 pts)
Renal faliure or Kidney failure ii. Partial credit: none
Based on his previous bouts with blue cheese addiction what do you think is the root cause of this disease? (4 pts)
Prolonged high blood pressure/hypertension (accept answers without prolonged) (3 pts), due to prolonged hypernatremia (1 pts). ii. Partial credit: None
How can we go about treating CJ? (4 pts, 2 pts per treatment, 1 bonus possible for addressing the root issue)

Dialysis (2 pts), kidney transplant (2 pts). ii. Bonus: Therapy to overcome his blue cheese addiction (1 bonus pt) iii. Partial credit: See point statement in question Diagram (8 pts, 1 for each correct fill in) Also accept muscle as an answer for muscularis Lymphatic MCQ

Remember that bus accident from Brenton’s case study? Ivory here was one of the passengers on that bus. She reports to the hospital with the other victims, but nurses notice she was bleeding a lot more than other patients, even though she didn’t have too much major trauma, just moderate cuts on her limbs/extremeties. She had no substantial damage to her abdomen or head. After she recovered from her topical injuries, she told doctors she’d been recently experiencing fever, chills, a loss of appetite, and lightheadedness ever since she ate some contaminated food before the accident. You decide to run a blood test and take away 2 notable findings. An abnormally low red blood cell count, and high levels of CRP.
potentialAnswers: What lymphatic disorder is Ivory struggling with, and what do you think caused it? (2 pts, 1 for disorder, 1 for cause) Please clearly indicate what you think is the condition and what you think is the cause.

Splenomegaly (1 pt), due to previous infection from the bad food (1 pt) ii. Full credit other conditions: Award full (2 pts) credit for mention of infection causing the splenomegaly, or for specifc bacterial/viral infection conditions as a causative factor for the splenomegaly ie. infective endocarditis, sepsis, etc. iii. DO NOT AWARD POINTS FOR “HYPERSPLENISM”.
What were 2 indicators from Ivory’s condition that helped to determine the cause of her disease/condition? (Max 4 pts, 2 pt each indicator)

Fever and chills as previous symptoms (2 pts), contaminated food she ate (1 pt), high levels of CRP in the blood test (2 pts). Award 4 points maximum. ii. Full credit other conditions: award indicator credit (2 pts) for a mention of fever or chills but do not count them as 2 separate indicators. Award indicator credit (1 pts) for food mention even if the contamination of the food is not mentioned.
How can we go about treating Ivory? (4 pts, 2 per treatment)

Treat her bacterial infection using antibiotics and manage the splenomegaly symptoms until it returns to normal size (2 pts), splenectomy (2 pts) ii. Full credit other conditions: Award treatment credit (2 pts) if the student claims there is no treatment for splenomegaly and to just treat symptoms until it returns to normal size. Diagram (14 pts, 1 for each correct fill in) Do not grade artery and vein.
